issues.legal_issue: Legal representatives substituted in a suit may raise available defences and file an additional written statement when they have a plausible interest in the property in dispute.
material_facts: A suit for specific performance was pending when the defendant died, and his legal representatives were brought on record.
The legal representatives sought permission to file an additional written statement and raise available defences.
A registered sale deed referred to the disputed property as purchased by the deceased and his sons, giving the sons a prima facie basis to claim an interest in it.
The lower courts rejected the application, preventing the legal representatives from presenting the defence and evidence.
issues.conclusion: The legal representatives were entitled to file an additional written statement and adduce evidence; whether their defence succeeds is for the trial court to decide.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22 Rule 4(2) CPC does not confine a legal representative to pleas appropriate only to that representative’s character as such. A party must have an opportunity to present a defence, consistently with natural justice and the CPC. The court relied on the registered sale deed as showing a prima facie interest, without finally deciding ownership.

rule.if: suit_for_specific_performance and defendant_died_during_suit and successors_joined_as_parties and successors_have_plausible_property_interest

predicates.suit_for_specific_performance: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.defendant_died_during_suit: The defendant died while the suit was pending.
predicates.successors_joined_as_parties: The deceased defendant’s successors were brought into the suit as parties.
predicates.successors_have_plausible_property_inter: The successors have a factual basis, such as a property document naming them as purchasers, for claiming an interest in the disputed property.
predicates.successors_may_file_additional_defence: The successors may file an additional written statement and present their available defence and evidence.

issues.definition: When a defendant dies during a specific-performance suit, successors who are joined as parties and have a plausible interest in the property may present an additional defence.

issues.legal_issue: A person seeking to join a suit for specific performance cannot be excluded merely because they are a third party to the contract if they show a fair semblance of title or interest in the property.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of an agreement concerning a shop.
A registered sale deed identified the deceased defendant and his sons as purchasers of the shop.
The deed provided a prima facie basis for the sons to claim an interest, although the court left the question of their ownership for the suit to decide.
The respondent relied on Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal to argue that third parties could not be added to a specific-performance suit.
issues.conclusion: Kasturi does not impose an absolute bar on impleading a third party in a specific-performance suit; a person showing a fair semblance of title or interest may apply to be impleaded.
issues.legal_principle: Order 1 Rule 10 CPC permits impleadment where a third party shows a fair semblance of title or interest; a mere busybody or interloper without such a basis cannot be added. Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal was distinguished because the decision does not bar impleadment of a person with such an interest. The court also relied on State of Orissa v. Sudhansu Sekhar Misra, Ambica Quarry Works v. State of Gujarat, Bhavnagar University v. Palitana Sugar Mills, and Bharat Petroleum Corporation v. N.R. Vairamani for the principle that precedents must be read in light of the facts they decide.

predicates.suit_for_specific_performance: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.nonparty_claims_property_interest: A person who is not a party to the agreement claims an interest in the property in dispute.
predicates.claim_has_fair_basis: The person points to facts or documents that provide a fair semblance of title or interest, rather than acting as a mere interloper.
predicates.nonparty_may_seek_impleadment: The person may apply to be joined as a party to the suit.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, a nonparty with a factually supported semblance of an interest in the property may seek to join the suit.
